notes.meaning: The angel Gabriel greets Mary with joy and announces that God has shown her special kindness. She is chosen to be the mother of the promised Savior, and the Lord is with her to protect and guide her. We can trust that God stays close to those He calls to serve Him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The greeting is understood to mean that Mary was filled with grace from her conception, preserving her from all sin throughout her life.

notes.meaning: Mary is surprised and troubled by the sudden appearance and words of the angel. She wonders what such an honoring message could mean for a simple, ordinary woman. When God's plans surprise us, it is natural to feel humble and amazed.

Gabriel tells Mary not to be afraid because she has found favor with God. This favor is God's grace, His free and undeserved love, rather than a reward for human merit. God brings peace to His people when He calls them to His service.

The angel announces that Mary will conceive and give birth to a son. She is told to name Him Jesus, a name that means the Lord saves. This child is the promised Savior sent to rescue His people from sin.

Gabriel reveals that Jesus will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High God. God will give Him the royal throne promised long ago to King David. His spiritual rule over God's people will never fail, and His kingdom will last forever.

Mary asks how this birth will happen since she is still an unmarried virgin. Her question does not come from doubt, but from an honest desire to understand God's plan. She trusts God's promise while wondering about the way it will take place.

The angel explains that the Holy Spirit will bring about the child's conception by God's direct power. Because of this divine miracle, the child will be completely holy and free from sin, rightly called the Son of God. God works in quiet, wonderful ways that go far beyond human ability.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Mary was prepared to bear the Son of God by being kept free from all stain of sin from the moment of her own conception.

notes.meaning: Gabriel gives Mary an encouraging sign by telling her that her relative Elizabeth is also expecting a baby. Though Elizabeth was very old and unable to have children, she was already six months pregnant. God often strengthens our faith by showing His kindness to others.

The angel assures Mary that nothing is impossible for God. Whatever the Lord has said and promised, He has the full power to perform. Believers can rest with complete confidence in God's unlimited strength.

Mary answers with quiet faith, calling herself the Lord's humble servant and welcoming His word. She submits completely to God's will, ready to face whatever difficulties may come. True faith trusts God's promises and surrenders to His purpose.

Mary quickly sets out on a journey of many miles to visit Elizabeth in the hill country of Judah. Traveling across the mountainous region took several days of hard walking. Her quick departure shows her eager desire to witness what God had done.

Mary enters the home of Zechariah the priest and warmly greets Elizabeth. The two women shared a special bond of love and a unique part in God's great work. Christian friendship is a sweet comfort when believers share what God is doing.

When Elizabeth hears Mary's voice, the unborn baby moves with joy inside her. At that moment, Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit and given prophetic insight. God was already preparing John to announce the coming Savior.

Led by the Holy Spirit, Elizabeth speaks with a loud voice to call Mary blessed among all women. She explains that Mary is blessed because the child she carries is the holy and divine Savior. Our true blessedness comes from our connection to Jesus Christ.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholics use this verse, along with verse 28, in teaching that Mary was without sin. Its words are also part of the Hail Mary prayer.

notes.meaning: Elizabeth humbly asks why such a great honor has been granted to her. She realizes that Mary is carrying her Lord, the divine King and Savior. A humble heart rejoices when God honors someone else.

Elizabeth tells Mary that her unborn child leaped for joy the second Mary spoke. This unusual movement was a sign confirming that the promised Messiah was present. Even before his birth, John began his work of pointing people to Jesus.

Elizabeth honors Mary for trusting what the Lord had spoken to her. Mary believed without demanding proof, knowing God would fulfill every promise He made. True happiness belongs to everyone who takes God at His word.

Mary begins a song of praise, declaring that her whole soul magnifies the Lord. To magnify God means to praise Him and make His greatness known to others. When our hearts are filled with God's goodness, praise pours out naturally.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: A few scholars have argued the song was really Elizabeth's, because a few old Latin copies give it to her. Most readers keep it as Mary's.

notes.meaning: Mary rejoices deeply in God as her Savior who rescues from sin and death. She celebrates her personal salvation even more than the outward honor of bearing the Messiah. Every believer shares this joy of being saved by God's grace.

Mary marvels that God noticed her lowly, humble condition instead of choosing the rich and powerful. Because of God's kindness, people throughout history will remember her as uniquely blessed. God tenderly cares for those who are humble and overlooked.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic tradition gives Mary further honor, with titles such as Queen of Heaven, and asks for her prayers.

notes.meaning: Mary praises the Almighty God for the wonderful miracles He has performed for her. She adds that His name is holy, meaning He is completely pure, just, and set apart from evil. All praise belongs to God when He acts with power in our lives.

Mary proclaims that God gives His mercy to everyone who fears Him throughout all generations. This fear is not terror, but a loving and deep reverence for God, like a child respecting a good father. God's tender mercy never ends for those who honor Him.

Mary pictures God's power as a mighty arm that wins great victories. He upsets the proud schemes of those who think they can succeed without Him. Human pride quickly crumbles before God's mighty strength.

God removes proud rulers from their high thrones and lifts up the lowly and humble. He turns worldly ideas of power upside down by honoring the weak. God delights to lift up those who know their need of Him.

God satisfies the hungry with good things, giving grace to those who crave His righteousness. But He sends away empty those who rely on their own wealth and feel no need for God. True spiritual satisfaction comes only to those who hunger for the Lord.
